title: On-call & Incident Response Playbook: Process, Runbooks, Postmortems, Rotations, Game Days, and Communications
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview
This playbook defines Redwood Inference’s standard on-call and incident response processes, canonical runbooks for common failure modes, postmortem expectations, rotation policies, game day guidance, and templates for public status page and customer communications. It is the single source of truth for engineers, SREs, and support leads during incidents.

Goals
- Restore customer-facing functionality and protect data integrity.
- Meet SLAs/SLOs and reduce MTTR through documented playbooks.
- Provide consistent, professional customer communication.
- Run recurring game days to validate runbooks and surface operational gaps.

Audience and scope
This document is intended for on-call engineers, SREs, incident commanders (ICs), on-call managers, customer success reps, and engineering managers. It covers Sev1/Sev2/Sev3 incidents that impact Redwood hosted API, Dedicated control plane, and Private deployment operations; it does not replace vendor-specific emergency procedures (e.g., cloud-provider status).

Incident severity definitions (table)
- SEV1 (P0): Wide-scale outage or critical data loss affecting >=20% of customers or core API unavailable for >2 minutes. Requires immediate IC escalation, all-hands response.
- SEV2 (P1): Significant degradation (high error rate or high latency) affecting a subset of customers or features; business impact but partial functionality remains.
- SEV3 (P2): Localized problem with limited impact, operational workarounds exist, or informational incidents.

On-call roles and responsibilities
- Pager: First responder for alerts in PagerDuty. Triage, gather telemetry, and follow runbook.
- Incident Commander (IC): Owns coordination, status updates, and decision authority for rollbacks/fallbacks. Usually senior SRE/owner for the affected service.
- Communications Lead: Drafts status page and customer comms; coordinates with Legal/PR for public messaging when required.
- Subject Matter Experts (SMEs): Component owners pulled in for debugging and mitigation.
- Postmortem Author: Responsible for writing the postmortem within the SLA window.

Alerting and escalation
1) Alerting: All production alerts should be configured in PagerDuty with clear runbook links and severity tags. Alerts must contain: service name, metric, threshold, one-line summary, runbook link, and suggested initial checks.
2) Escalation policy: Default escalation path: primary on-call (5 minutes), secondary on-call (10 minutes), Pager duty schedule owner (15 minutes), IC (20 minutes). Customize per-service where required.

Incident lifecycle (step-by-step)
1) Detect & Acknowledge (0-5 min): Pager acknowledges alert, opens incident channel (slack #inc-<service>-<incident-id>), and posts initial one-line summary with timestamp.
2) Triage (0-10 min): Run initial checks from runbook (see Runbook section). If SEV1 or unresolved in 15 minutes, escalate to IC.
3) Declare Incident & Notify (IC): IC declares severity, sets timeline, informs leadership and support, and posts to status page as "investigating" for SEV1/SEV2.
4) Mitigate & Restore: Apply mitigations in runbook (circuit breaker, rollback, route failover). Prioritize customer-visible recovery over full root cause.
5) Stabilize & Monitor: Verify metrics and logs show recovery; keep customers informed at regular cadence.
6) Post-incident: IC closes active response after stabilization; initiates postmortem within 48 hours.

Runbooks (canonical checks and mitigations)
Include exact CLI and console checks, prioritization, and rollback actions. Each runbook entry should be a short actionable checklist. Example runbooks below: 

A) API 5xx spike (text-generation API)
- Initial checks (5 mins):
  - Check service health: curl -sS https://api.redwood.ai/health | jq .status
  - Query metrics: dashboards -> /dashboards/api-errors : 5xx rate over 5m
  - Check queue/backpressure metrics and GPU utilization (prometheus queries provided in dashboards)
- Mitigation steps (10-30 mins):
  1. Enable circuit breaker for non-critical endpoints: /admin/api/circuit-breaker enable --service gen --threshold 0.05
  2. Scale up inference pool (if Dedicated/hosted): terraform apply -var="scale_inference=true" OR trigger autoscaler via console
  3. If recent deploy in last 30 minutes, roll back to last-good version: deploy rollback --service gen --to "v2026-01-12-rc"
  4. If KV cache pressure observed, clear prefix caches for affected model: redis-cli DEL <prefix-key>
- Post-mitigation: validate 5xx reduced to baseline and remove circuit breakers after stability window (30m).

B) Controller / Orchestration failure (control plane degraded)
- Initial checks:
  - Check k8s control plane: kubectl get pods -n platform --field-selector=status.phase!=Running
  - Check platform API latencies and error logs in ElasticSearch
- Mitigation:
  1. Failover to alternate control-plane region if configured: platform-failover --target region-us-west-2
  2. If database is degraded, enable read-only mode for non-essential endpoints: db-maintenance --mode readonly
  3. Engage DB on-call and run DB checksum/repair steps per DB runbook

C) Private deployment customer outage (onprem)
- Runbook priority: customer SLA first; if no remote access, escalate to Support/Customer Success to coordinate on-site work.
- Steps: confirm connectivity, collect support bundle (support-collect --target <customer-id>), provide temporary hosted fallback if contract allows.

Runbook hygiene and ownership
- Each service must have a runbook page with: purpose, owner, contact list (PagerDuty schedule), CLI checks, mitigation steps, rollback commands, post-incident verification steps, and known false-positives.
- Owners must review runbooks quarterly and after any incident or deploy that changes behavior.

Postmortem and RCA process
- Trigger: postmortem required for SEV1/SEV2 with customer impact >1 hour or SEV1 regardless of duration.
- Timeline:
  - Draft created by Postmortem Author within 48 hours.
  - Initial draft review: within 5 business days by reviewers and IC.
  - Finalized postmortem published within 10 business days with action items assigned.
- Template fields (must be present as plain headings in the postmortem):
  - Title, incident id, severity, services impacted, start/end timestamps, detection method, timeline of events (minute-granular), impact summary, root cause, contributing factors, mitigations applied, corrective actions (with owner and ETA), customer communication timeline, lessons learned, and verification plan.
- Blameless culture: Focus on systemic fixes, not individuals. If human error is a primary cause, include improved guardrails and automation to reduce risk.

Action tracking and follow-up
- Create Jira tickets for corrective actions with label "incident-action" and link back to postmortem.
- Track action completion in monthly reliability reviews; owners must update status in the postmortem until resolved.

On-call rotations and expectations
- Weekly primary rotation for SREs (7-day shift) with backup rotation; engineering teams may run 24/7 PagerDuty schedules depending on product ownership.
- Handover checklist (for shift changes): current incidents, recent alerts, outstanding action items, and scheduled maintenance. Handover must be posted in rotation channel and acknowledged.
- Overtime and compensation: See People Ops on-call compensation policy (link to People Ops page).

Game days and validation exercises
- Frequency: Quarterly company-wide game days; monthly team-level exercises for critical services.
- Objectives: Validate runbook accuracy, measure MTTR, exercise cross-team coordination, test public communications cadence.
- Example exercise: simulated SEV1 API outage with injected 5xx errors; measure time to detection, time to mitigation, and status update cadence.
- After-action review: Game days produce a short report with findings, action items, and runbook updates.

Status page and customer communication templates
- Status page states: operational, investigating, degraded, partial_outage, major_outage, maintenance. Use consistent language and timestamps in UTC.
- Short status page templates (examples):
  *Initial (Acknowledgement):* "We are investigating elevated error rates impacting the Text Generation API. Our engineers are actively diagnosing. We will provide updates every 30 minutes or as new information becomes available. (Start time: 2026-02-15T15:03Z)"
  *Update (Mitigation applied):* "Mitigation in progress: circuit breaker enabled for non-critical endpoints and additional capacity being provisioned. Error rates reduced from 12% to 3% over the last 10 minutes. Next update in 30 minutes. (Update time: 2026-02-15T15:35Z)"
  *Resolved:* "Issue resolved: full service restored and verified. Root cause investigation underway; a postmortem will be published within five business days. (Resolved at: 2026-02-15T16:12Z)"
- Customer email templates (initial, update, resolution)
  *Initial acknowledgement (example):*
  Subject: Redwood Inference — Incident affecting Text Generation API
  Body: Hello <CustomerName>,
  We are aware of elevated error rates impacting the Text Generation API since 2026-02-15T15:03Z. Our engineering team is actively investigating. We will provide updates every 30 minutes. For status, visit https://status.redwood.ai. If you need a dedicated update, reply to this message and we will escalate.

  *Update (example):*
  Subject: Redwood Inference — Update on Text Generation API incident
  Body: Hello <CustomerName>,
  We have applied mitigations (circuit breaker, capacity scale-up). Error rates improved from 12% to 3%. We continue to monitor. Expected next update in 30 minutes.

  *Resolution (example):*
  Subject: Redwood Inference — Incident resolved (Text Generation API)
  Body: Hello <CustomerName>,
  The incident affecting the Text Generation API is resolved as of 2026-02-15T16:12Z. Service has been validated and is operating within normal parameters. A postmortem will be shared when finalized. We apologize for the disruption.

Status page operational guidance (tech notes)
- Status page entries must be created/updated by the Communications Lead or delegated on-call. Record UTC timestamps and add incident ID. Avoid speculative language.
- If customer data or security is affected, escalate to Security & Compliance and change confidentiality to "restricted" per policy.

Measurement and KPIs
- Key metrics tracked per incident: Time to detect, Time to Acknowledge, Time to Mitigate (customer-visible), Time to Resolve, Number of customers impacted, SLA breach flag.
- Quarterly reliability review dashboard aggregates incident counts, average MTTR, and open action items by team.

Templates and checklists (quick copy)
- Incident channel creation: #inc-<service>-<YYYYMMDD>-<seq>
- Slack pinned items: incident playbook link, runbook link, status page link, PagerDuty incident URL
- Postmortem checklist: draft within 48h, reviewers assigned, Jira actions created, RCA and verification plan present

Appendix: Common tooling and useful commands
- PagerDuty: https://redwood.pagerduty.com (incidents > create > link runbook)
- Support bundle: support-collect --service <service> --since <timestamp> > /tmp/support-<id>.tgz
- Prometheus query examples: increase(http_requests_total{job="api"}[5m]) / increase(http_requests_total[5m])
- Kibana query examples: service:"api" AND level:ERROR AND @timestamp:[now-15m TO now]

Document ownership and maintenance
- Owner (oncall-and-incident-response): Maya Chen (document owner).
- Review cadence: Annual mandatory review and after any SEV1 incident.
